reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs with no comment, which is exactly what is expected for a compliant finding — no over-flagging.

The cited text supports the preferred position from our (IBM/Customer) side: §13.1 (p0197) has MSL assign all IP in hardware, software, design and documentation of delivered Products to IBM; p0198 extends IBM ownership plus assignment to MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes; §13.3(a) (p0208) bars any grant of rights in IBM pre-existing IP other than a narrow royalty-free confidential-information licence solely to manufacture for IBM.

No assignment of Customer IP or data to the Vendor and no joint ownership appears in the cited paragraphs; MSL's retained use right is limited to performing its obligations, and it is barred from using proprietary assembly/test processes — so no walk-away trigger. The deterministic check ('no assignment of Customer Data/IP to Vendor remains') is consistent.

Supporting provisions cited are directionally correct: p1105 (IBM-paid tooling becomes and remains IBM property) and p1530 (IBM retains title to all Loaned Items; MSL may not transfer) reinforce Customer ownership rather than undercut it.

The two shortfalls (no express licence-back of MSL background IP embedded in Products; no standalone Customer Data ownership sentence) are correctly treated as minor sub-elements noted in the rationale rather than raised as deviations, consistent with the classification semantics.
